text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Compared to coffee sugar is a dull affair and white sugar futures showed little inclination to do anything but tread water. A lackluster performance on the raws market ensured that premium movements were limited, deterring sellers waiting at $69 and above on the May arbitrage and leaving London's nearby spreads trapped in a range.

May closed $0.90 higher at $308.00 per tonne, while August added $0.30 to close at $306.00 per tonne. Raw sugar futures in New York closed mostly higher in quiet trade. There was no fresh news to influence prices. May rose 7 points to close at 10.93 cents/lb, while July closed 1 point higher at 10.68 cents/lb.
Without fresh fundamental news prices are likely to remain within the current trading range.

EUROPEAN UNION - EU carry-over of non-quota C sugar to the 1997/98 marketing season is expected to total 917,000 tonnes, white value, up from 900,000 tonnes estimated on February 3 and 685,000 tonnes in 1995/96. The Commission also raised its forecast of C sugar exports to 2.44 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from 1.58 million tonnes the previous year.

The revisions are the result of a higher than expected crop this season. Total beet sugar production in 1996/97 is now estimated at 16.521 million tonnes, white value, up from the previous estimate of 15.564 million tonnes and 15.56 million tonnes in 1995/96.
THAILAND - Thai sugar production during November/March 4, reached 4.366 million tonnes, raw value, up from 4.338 million tonnes produced the same period in 1995/96.

Although the amount surpassed that of the previous season, the rise was caused mostly by increased capacity but yield still trailed that posted in 1995/96. The yield was recorded at 100.98 kg of sugar per tonne of cane vs 104.40 kg last season.

BELGIUM-LUXEMBOURG - Sugar imports in November 1996 amounted to 69,173 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 129,147 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first two months of 1996/97 (October/November) up to 118,160 tonnes against 166,152 tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1995/96 reached 659,840 tonnes compared to 1.139 million tonnes in 1994/95 and 663,985 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in October/November 1996 were France with 77,896 tonnes whites against 139,334 tonnes and Germany with 37,428 tonnes compared to 22,613 tonnes.

Sugar exports in November 1996 amounted to 114,223 tonnes against 166,648 tonnes in November 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/November 1996 up to 208,669 tonnes compared to 347,663 tonnes in October/November 1995. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 989,122 tonnes against 1.566 million tonnes in 1994/95.

Major countries of destination in October/November 1996 were Syria with 25,674 tonnes whites, down from 60,744 tonnes, Algeria with 22,191 tonnes, up from 4,348 tonnes and Turkey with 17,493 tonnes compared to 46,803 tonnes.

UNITED STATES - Sugar imports in December 1996 amounted to 155,898 tonnes, raw value, up from last year's 72,387 tonnes. This brought cumulative imports in the first quarter of 1996/97 (October/December) up to 478,366 tonnes against 306,064 tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total imports in 1995/96 reached 2.615 million tonnes compared to 1.557 million tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in October/December 1996 were Australia with 63,311 tonnes raws against 30,000 tonnes, the Philippines with 60,344 tonnes compared to nil, Peru with 49,750 tonnes against 40,539 tonnes and Brazil with 40,253 tonnes compared to 19,210 tonnes.

Sugar exports in December 1996 dropped to 7,003 tonnes, down from 30,693 tonnes in December 1995. This brought cumulative exports in October/December 1996 up to 50,328 tonnes compared to 104,345 tonnes in 1995. Total exports in 1995/96 reached 310,341 tonnes compared to 504,854 tonnes in 1994/95.
Major countries of destination in October/December 1996 were Jamaica with 8,706 tonnes whites against 11,544 tonnes and Peru with 8,191 tonnes compared to 13,288 tonnes.
